Please reference `@.agents/memories/20-tooling.md` as needed.

As this project's AI coding tool, you must follow the additional conventions below, in addition to the built-in functions.

`.rulesync/` is the source of truth. Author changes in `rules`, `skills`, `subagents`, `commands`, `hooks`, and `mcp` there first. Generated target directories and prompt files are build artifacts; regenerate them from RuleSync instead of editing them by hand. Keep shared root `AGENTS.md` content in this overview rule and follow-up split rules off AGENTS-writing targets. Fix `.rulesync/` when generated output looks wrong, then re-run `rulesync`.

`rules`: always-on guidance, routing, cross-cutting constraints. `skills`: reusable domain knowledge and standards. `subagents`: named specialists with bounded scope and tool budgets. `commands`: user-invocable entry points; prefer local runtime. `hooks`: advisory, portable reminders/automation. `mcp`: shared MCP registrations and transport metadata.

Keep frontmatter strictly RuleSync-compliant; add target-specific blocks only for real runtime differences. Keep commands deterministic, hooks advisory, and route hook-only targets through generated rules or hook text instead of unavailable skill or command surfaces.

Validate and regenerate with the system-wide `rulesync` binary: use `rulesync generate --check` as the consistency gate, then `rulesync generate` when changes are intentional. Review source and generated diffs together; do not hand-edit generated target directories to patch a platform quirk. **Verify target configurations** using the per-target checklists in `.rulesync/verification/` before committing changes.

Compatible targets include GitHub Copilot CLI; target support is intentionally asymmetric. Author shared behavior once; use target-specific blocks only where runtime differs. This toolkit is distributed via RuleSync.

Tab cycles **primary** agents only. `<REDACTED_USER>` invokes subagents. `dotnet-architect` is a primary OpenCode agent in this toolkit and can appear in Tab rotation. Gemini CLI inherits shared .NET session routing and thin post-edit Roslyn, formatting, and Slopwatch advisories from `.rulesync/hooks.json`. Factory Droid uses generated rules and hooks for .NET session and MCP routing; keep reminders compatible with its rules-plus-hooks surface, without imported skills or commands.

If RuleSync reports `Multiple root rulesync rules found`, ensure only one root overview rule exists. Use RuleSync commands directly instead of manually reproducing catalog, prompt, incident, or graph logic from source.
